newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia cen.bank cuts non-resident T-bill yield.
newsitem.headline: Russia cen.bank cuts non-resident T-bill yield.

text.p: Russia's central bank will cut the guaranteed yield for foreign holders on government securities to 9.0 percent from 11.0 percent effective July 15, the bank said in a statement on Monday.
The yield which is basically guaranteed through forward rouble contracts is effectively a minimum yield, and non-residents who actively trade bills can reap higher profits.

Terms for the forward contracts which guarantee the dollar yield are being loosened this year as part of Russia's plan to put foreign and domestic investors of rouble-denominated government securities on an equal footing.
By January 1, 1998, all forward contract requirements will be dropped.

Rouble-denominated yields have fallen sharply over the last year to near 19 percent, largely on increased participation by foreigners in the approximately $50 billion market, Russia's largest and most liquid domestic market.
Rouble yields were close to 30 percent at the beginning of May and 200 percent a year ago during the presidential election campaign.
